009/**
010 * Provides shared helpers for activity category parsing, greeting generation,
011 * username storage, and search filtering. Methods are static so callers can use
012 * them without creating a utility instance.
013 */
014public class DayPlannerUtils {
015    /**
016     * Retrieves the username from file, prompting the user (and storing the new
017     * name to file) if no name is currently stored.
018     * 
019     * @param dirName  Name of the data directory.
020     * @param fileName Name of the username file.
021     * @param keyboard Input instance to use to enter new username if necessary.
022     * @return The stored name, or a newly entered name when no usable file value
023     *         exists.
024     */
025    public static String getUsername(String dirName, String fileName, Input keyboard) {
026        String name = "exception"; // fall back name in case of error
027
028        // Case 1: file doesn't exist
029        if (!FileUtils.exists(dirName, fileName)) {
030            System.out.println("\n\nHello new user, please enter your name:");
031            name = keyboard.readString();
032
033            try {
034                FileUtils.writeText(dirName, fileName, name);
035            } catch (Exception e) {
036                System.out.println("Couldn't write name to file.");
037            }
038
039            return name;
040        }
041
042        // Case 2: File exists
043        try {
044            name = FileUtils.readFirstLine(dirName, fileName);
045        } catch (Exception e) {
046            System.out.println("Couldn't read name from file.");
047        }
048
049        return name;
050    }
051
052
053
054    /**
055     * Generates a multi-line time-appropriate greeting and activity summary for the
056     * user. Each line of the greeting is indented by 1 tab.
057     * 
058     * @param username            The user's name.
059     * @param numActivities       The current number of activities.
060     * @return Formatted greeting string indented by 1 tab.
061     */
062    public static String getGreeting(String username, int numActivities) {
063        int hour = LocalTime.now().getHour();
064        String greeting;
065
066        if (hour < 12)      greeting = "Good morning";
067        else if (hour < 17) greeting = "Good afternoon";
068        else                greeting = "Good evening";
069
070        String text = "\t%s, %s!\n\tYou have %d activities currently entered.";
071        return String.format(text, greeting, username, numActivities);
072    }
073
074
075
076    /**
077     * Deletes the stored username file if it exists. This is used by the hidden
078     * maintenance command; it does not prompt for or create a replacement name.
079     * 
080     * @param dirName  Name of the data directory.
081     * @param fileName Name of the username file.
082     */
083    public static void flushUsername(String dirName, String fileName) {
084        try {
085            FileUtils.delete(dirName, fileName);
086            System.out.println("Done, although username isn't refreshed until program is relaunched");
087        } catch (Exception e) {
088            e.printStackTrace();
089        }
090    }
091
092
093
094    /**
095     * <p>
096     * Determines whether an activity satisfies the specified search criteria.
097     * </p>
098     * <p>
099     * All non-null criteria must be satisfied simultaneously:
100     * </p>
101     * <ul>
102     * <li><b>searchStart</b>: the activity's start time must be &gt;=
103     * <code>searchStart</code>.</li>
104     * <li><b>searchEnd</b>: the activity's end time must be &lt;=
105     * <code>searchEnd</code>.</li>
106     * </ul>
107     * <p>
108     * Passing <code>null</code> for any filter disables that filter entirely.
109     * </p>
110     * 
111     * @param act         The activity to test.
112     * @param type        If valid {@link dayplanner.ActivityType}, then
113     *                    <code>act</code> must be an instance of this type. Value
114     *                    of <code>null</code> indicates to not filter by type.
115     * @param searchStart Minimum start time, or <code>null</code> for open start.
116     * @param searchEnd   Maximum end time, or <code>null</code> for open end.
117     * @return <code>true</code> if the activity satisfies all given criteria,
118     *         <code>false</code> otherwise.
119     */
120    public static boolean matchesCriteria(Activity act, ActivityType type, Time searchStart, Time searchEnd) {
121        // if no activity was given, there is nothing to check
122        if (act == null)
123            return false;
124
125        // check type
126        if (type != null && !act.getType().equals(type))
127            return false;
128
129        // check start time
130        // a must start on or after the lower bound
131        if (searchStart != null && act.getStartTime().compareTo(searchStart) < 0)
132            return false;
133
134        // check end time
135        // a must end on or before the upper bound
136        if (searchEnd != null && act.getEndTime().compareTo(searchEnd) > 0)
137            return false;
138
139        return true;
140    }
141    
142

144    /**
145     * Prompts the user for a time period filter and parses the start and end times.
146     * A blank response means both bounds are open; a single hyphen may introduce
147     * either one-sided range, for example {@code 2026/09/12 06:00 -}.
148     * 
149     * @param keyboard Input instance to use to prompt the user
150     * @return A two-element array {@code {searchStart, searchEnd}}; either element
151     *         may be null to represent an open bound.
152     */
153    public static Time[] readTimePeriod(Input keyboard) {
154        System.out.println("Enter a time period (e.g. '2026/9/12, 6:00 - 2026/9/22, 11:59', '2026/9/12, 6:00 -', '- 2026/9/22, 11:59'), or press Enter for any time:");
155        String line = keyboard.readString();
156
157        // if the user typed nothing, both sides of the range should be unrestricted
158        if (line.isEmpty())
159            return new Time[] { null, null };
160
161        // find at what index the dash is typed
162        // all common dash characters are accepted
163        int dashIndex = -1;
164        char[] dashes = { '-', '–', '—' };
165        for (char d : dashes) {
166            dashIndex = line.indexOf(d);
167            if (dashIndex != -1)
168                break;
169        }
170
171        // if the user actually did type a dash...
172        if (dashIndex != -1) {
173            // convert the input into two time instances
174            String part1 = line.substring(0, dashIndex).trim();
175            String part2 = line.substring(dashIndex + 1).trim();
176            Time start = part1.isEmpty() ? null : Input.parseTime(part1);
177            Time end = part2.isEmpty() ? null : Input.parseTime(part2);
178
179            // and only parse a boundary if the user typed one properly
180            if (!part1.isEmpty() && start == null) {
181                System.out.println("Invalid starting time. Use format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM. Try again:");
182                return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
183            }
184            if (!part2.isEmpty() && end == null) {
185                System.out.println("Invalid ending time. Use format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM. Try again:");
186                return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
187            }
188
189            // ensure that start comes first
190            if (start != null && end != null && start.compareTo(end) >= 0) {
191                System.out.println("Starting time must be before ending time. Try again:");
192                return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
193            }
194
195            return new Time[] { start, end };
196        }
197
198        // if the user didn't input a dash...
199        // then a single valid time is treated as the lower bound with no upper bound
200        Time single = Input.parseTime(line);
201        if (single != null)
202            return new Time[] { single, null };
203
204        // if we got here then nothing else worked
205        System.out.println("Invalid time period. Expected 'start - end', 'start -', '- end', or press Enter to skip. Try again:");
206        return readTimePeriod(keyboard);
207    }
208

212     * Default constructor for DayPlannerUtils.
213     */
214    private DayPlannerUtils() {}
